item.aggregated_output:
---
name: project-setup
description: 'Sets up Toolkit V2 in a new project or repairs one: copies the model scaffold, applies tracker, memory, and Salesforce answers, and fixes this Mac, Notion, or Hindsight. Use when the owner says "set up Toolkit V2", "set up this project", "check the setup", "update the toolkit", or "new computer".'
---

# Project setup

Voice: write to the owner in plain English. Claude Code: follow the project's Plain English output style. Codex: follow the "How to write replies" section of `AGENTS.md`.
The interview wording and what setup installs: `references/interview.md`. Repair, switching, new computer, and wiring: `references/repair-and-wiring.md`. Put each `toolkit` command on its own line.

## Steps

1. Check the setup. If `toolkit` is not found, run `node <this skill's folder>/../../bin/toolkit machine-setup` (the skill's folder is the one holding this file). If doctor reports a computer problem, run machine-setup. Name anything the owner must do himself: `ntn login` opens a browser sign-in; trusting the hooks in Codex happens in its `/hooks` screen. Never do those for him. This skill sets up Toolkit V2, never the older claude-toolkit (its `project-init` skill); when the owner names Toolkit V2 and only `project-init` is listed, say so and use this skill's steps.
   `toolkit doctor`
   `toolkit machine-setup`
2. No `.toolkit.json`: a new project. Look before asking: an empty or existing repository; `sfdx-project.json` answers the Salesforce question in advance. Then ask one question at a time, each with a recommendation, in this order: the project name (with its key, id prefix, and owner name, confirmed in one line); the tracker (local folders, Notion, GitHub Issues, Jira); the memory (built-in `.memory/`, local Hindsight, Notion); Salesforce or not, and for Salesforce the sandbox and production org aliases; whether he wants `SOUL.md` (a no becomes `--decline SOUL.md`, so no later sync brings it back).
3. Run init with the answers (the second line, with `--salesforce`, for a Salesforce project; add `--decline SOUL.md` after a no). Setup copies the model scaffold and applies your answers: it copies the model project's folders and files, keeps only the blocks of `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, and `PROJECT.md` that match the answers, fills the project name, writes the rules list and `.toolkit.json`, installs the tracker, memory, and Salesforce parts only when chosen, never copies work items or memory records, and turns the V2 plugins on and every `*@claude-toolkit` plugin off in this project. Then record the choices init has no flag for: the id prefix when it is not `WI`, and the Salesforce org aliases. With Notion, init may take another id prefix when `WI` is already used there: say the prefix it reports in one line. In Codex: init writes `.codex/` and `.agents/`, which the Codex sandbox refuses, and it writes them first. Before running it, tell the owner that Codex will ask to run it outside the sandbox. If it stops with "Could not write ... .codex/" (or `.agents/`), nothing else was written: stop, show him the exact command init printed, and ask him to approve it or to run it in a terminal. Never change a setup answer (hosts, tracker, memory, Salesforce) to get past an error, and never set it up in another folder and copy it over.
   `toolkit init --name "<name>" --key <key> --tracker <tracker> --memory <memory> --owner "<owner>"`
   `toolkit init --name "<name>" --key <key> --tracker <tracker> --memory <memory> --owner "<owner>" --salesforce`
   `toolkit config set tracker.idPrefix <prefix>`
   `toolkit config set salesforce.orgs.sandbox <alias>`
   `toolkit config set salesforce.orgs.production <alias>`
4. Wire the choices. Notion: check the sign-in with `ntn whoami` (if it fails, the owner runs `ntn login` himself), then build the project's pages. Hindsight: check the service (install or start it only after a yes), then create the project's bank. GitHub or Jira: show the written instructions and create nothing in that service without a yes. Salesforce: fill the API version, which the model leaves as `XX.0`. Read it from the sandbox org (the `apiVersion` field of the read-only `sf org display -o <sandbox alias> --json`), or ask the owner. Put it in `sfdx-project.json` (`sourceApiVersion`) and in the `<version>` line of `delivery/deployment/full-project-deployment-template/package.xml`; the work item templates get it when `sf-component-tracker` copies them.
   `toolkit notion ensure-root`
   `toolkit notion ensure-project --project-name "<name>"`
   `toolkit hindsight service status`
   `toolkit hindsight ensure-bank`
5. Fill the setup guides: the copied files carry fill-in guide comments and `<angle bracket>` prompts. Fill them only with facts the owner confirmed (the one-sentence outcome and the "Build, test, or deploy" row in `AGENTS.md`, then `PROJECT.md` and `README.md`; `PROJECT-ROADMAP.md` and `requirements/SYSTEM-DATA-MODEL.md` when the facts are known), fill `SOUL.md` with his words when he wanted it, and delete each guide once its file is filled. List any prompt left for a fact nobody knows yet, including those in `PROJECT-ROADMAP.md` and `requirements/SYSTEM-DATA-MODEL.md`. A `SOUL.md` the owner turns down after init: record the no with the command below, then delete the file, so sync and doctor leave it out.
   `toolkit config set declined SOUL.md`
6. `.toolkit.json` present: repair. Show one numbered table from doctor and the dry run: missing, out of date, changed by the owner, broken wiring, each with its fix. Run sync only after a yes; it adds every missing file at once and never overwrites a file the project changed. Report a changed file as "project ahead of the toolkit".
   `toolkit sync --dry-run`
   `toolkit sync`
7. Switching memory: export from the old backend, change the choice, add its files, wire the new backend (step 4), check the import with a dry run, then import. Switching tracker: no command does it in this version; show a preview and move items only with the owner's yes.
   `toolkit memory export --to <backup-folder>/memory`
   `toolkit config set memory.type <memory>`
   `toolkit sync`
   `toolkit memory import --from <backup-folder>/memory --dry-run`
   `toolkit memory import --from <backup-folder>/memory`
8. Run doctor until it is clean, then show the first briefing. The setup files are not committed yet, and the first merge of a work item needs them committed: offer one commit of the files setup added or changed, staged by name (never `git add -A`), and make it only after a yes (in Codex, Codex asks him again to run `git commit` outside the sandbox). Explain in plain words what was set up, what was skipped, whether it is committed, what the owner must do himself, and one next step ("Tell me the first thing you want built.").
   `toolkit brief`

## Steps only the owner can do

Say each one plainly, with why, and wait. Never do them for him.

- **`ntn login`**: signs the Notion command-line tool into his Notion account. It opens a browser sign-in. Needed only for a Notion tracker or Notion memory, and only when `ntn whoami` fails.
- **Trust the hooks in Codex**: open Codex in this project, type `/hooks`, and trust the Toolkit V2 hooks. Codex skips plugin hooks until he does. Needed again after the hooks change or the project folder moves.
- **Start a new session** after setup, so Claude Code loads the new settings and the Plain English style.
- **Approve Codex running the init command outside its sandbox**, when setup runs inside Codex, or run the command init printed in a terminal.
- **Start a new project from Codex:** Codex lists the Toolkit V2 skills only in a project that `toolkit init` has set up, because the V2 plugins are on only where a project's `.codex/config.toml` turns them on. In a new folder, run `toolkit init` in a terminal first (or set the project up from Claude Code), then open Codex there and say "finish setting up Toolkit V2".

## Rules

- One question per message. Every question carries a recommendation and its main reason.
- Every step is safe to run again. When a step fails, fix the cause and run it again; init writes `.toolkit.json` last, and a second run records the files an earlier run wrote.
- Never change an answer the owner gave (tracker, memory, hosts, Salesforce, `SOUL.md`) to get past a failed command. Stop, say what failed, and say what he must approve or run.
- Nothing is created outside this project without a yes: no GitHub repository, no Jira fields, no paid service, no Notion pages outside the "AI Agent Second Brain" page.
- Instruction files follow the model: `AGENTS.md` holds the instructions, and one root `CLAUDE.md` (installed when Claude Code is a host) holds only the line `@AGENTS.md`, so Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md` through it. Doctor checks this. There is no other `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, or `CLAUDE.local.md`. Because the root `CLAUDE.md` exists, Claude Code does not load a subfolder's `AGENTS.md` by itself; the root `AGENTS.md` tells the agent to read it before editing in that folder. Ask before changing or removing a `CLAUDE.md` the owner wrote.

# Repair, switching, a new computer, and wiring

Detail for `project-setup` steps 1 and 4 to 7.

## Reaching the `toolkit` command

- Claude Code puts the plugin's `bin/` folder on the path, so `toolkit` works
  in every Claude Code session.
- Codex needs the small wrapper script that `toolkit machine-setup` writes at
  `~/.local/bin/toolkit`. When `toolkit` is not found, run the plugin's copy
  directly once: `node <this skill's folder>/../../bin/toolkit machine-setup`.
  The skill's folder is the folder that holds `SKILL.md`; both hosts show that
  path when they load the skill.
- Node 20 or later is required. When `node --version` is older or missing,
  tell the owner and ask before installing it.

## Wiring Notion

Needed when the tracker or the memory is `notion`.

1. `ntn whoami`. When it fails, the owner runs `ntn login` himself: it opens a
   browser sign-in to his Notion account. Wait for him to say it is done, then
   run `ntn whoami` again.
2. `toolkit notion ensure-root` checks the "AI Agent Second Brain" page and
   the Projects database, and adds what is missing.
3. `toolkit notion ensure-project --project-name "<name>"` creates or repairs
   this project's row, its Work Items database (board and table views, the
   fourteen stages, sub-items), its Memory database, and its focus and
   glossary pages. It saves the Notion ids in `.toolkit.json`.
4. Both commands only add. They never delete or trash anything, and they
   refuse to write outside the "AI Agent Second Brain" page.
5. In Codex, Notion calls need the network, which Codex's sandbox turns off.
   The project's `.codex/rules/toolkit.rules` lets `toolkit` commands run
   outside the sandbox; when it is missing, Codex asks the owner to approve
   each call.

## Wiring Hindsight

Needed when the memory is `hindsight`. Hindsight runs only on this Mac, never
in Hindsight Cloud, and never in Docker.

1. `toolkit hindsight health`: the local server at `127.0.0.1:8888` answers.
2. When it does not: `toolkit hindsight service status`. Not installed: ask,
   then `toolkit hindsight service install`. Installed but stopped: ask, then
   `toolkit hindsight service start`.
3. The server uses the local model `gpt-oss:20b` through Ollama. When doctor
   says Ollama is not running, tell the owner; it runs as a Homebrew service
   (`brew services start ollama`), which he may prefer to start himself.
4. `toolkit hindsight ensure-bank` creates this project's memory bank (one
   bank per project, named by the project key) and saves it in
   `.toolkit.json`.

## GitHub Issues or Jira

- Show the owner the written instructions. In a GitHub or Jira project, any
  `toolkit work` command exits with code 3 and prints their path, for
  example `toolkit work list`. They are the work plugin's
  `references/trackers/github.md` and `references/trackers/jira.md`.
- GitHub: creating the stage, type, priority, and approval labels needs his
  yes. Never create a GitHub repository without his yes.
- Jira: the Stage field or labels and the status map need his yes and, often,
  a Jira admin. Record the status map as a `DECISIONS.md` row with
  `toolkit decision add`, saved with `publish-docs`.

## Repair (`.toolkit.json` present)

1. `toolkit doctor` lists every problem with its fix.
2. `toolkit sync --dry-run` lists the scaffold files that are missing or out
   of date against the model copy in the toolkit, and the files the project
   changed on purpose.
3. Show one numbered table:

   | # | Problem | Kind | Fix |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | 1 | `.claude/rules/keep-work-item-current.md` is missing | missing | `toolkit sync` |
   | 2 | `AGENTS.md` differs from the toolkit's version | changed by the owner | none: project ahead of the toolkit |
   | 3 | Notion Memory database is missing | broken wiring | `toolkit notion ensure-project` |

4. `toolkit sync` applies every sync row at once. When the owner declines one
   of them, say so and ask whether to run sync anyway or skip it. Wiring rows
   are fixed one at a time with their own command, after his yes.
5. A file the project changed on purpose is never overwritten. Report it as
   "project ahead of the toolkit".
6. Run `toolkit doctor` again until it is clean.

## Updating the toolkit

- "Update the toolkit" usually means bringing this project up to date with
  the installed toolkit: the repair steps above. When the owner changed his
  model project, the toolkit's copy of the model is refreshed first, in the
  toolkit's own repository; a project sees the change only after the updated
  plugins are installed.
- When doctor says the installed plugins are older than the toolkit source,
  the plugins themselves need updating first. In Claude Code, with the
  owner's yes: `claude plugin marketplace update toolkit-v2`, then
  `claude plugin update <plugin>@toolkit-v2` for each plugin. Then start a
  new session and run the repair steps.
- Changed hooks must be trusted again in Codex (`/hooks`). That is the
  owner's step.

## Switching the memory backend

The memory export and import commands move memory between backends. The
project-wide `toolkit export` and `toolkit import` do not: they copy only the
local `.work-items/` and `.memory/` folders, so they would miss Hindsight and
Notion memory.

1. `toolkit memory export --to <backup-folder>/memory` copies every record
   (retired ones too), the current focus, and the glossary from the current
   backend to Markdown files. Run it before changing anything. Use the
   owner's backup folder, outside the project.
2. `toolkit config set memory.type <builtin|hindsight|notion>`.
3. `toolkit sync` adds the files the new backend needs (for example the
   `.memory/` seeds for built-in memory).
4. Wire the new backend (Notion or Hindsight above).
5. `toolkit memory import --from <backup-folder>/memory --dry-run` lists what
   would be saved and any file that breaks a rule. Show it to the owner.
6. `toolkit memory import --from <backup-folder>/memory` saves it into the new
   backend. A record with the same key is replaced.
7. `toolkit memory status` and `toolkit doctor` confirm it.
8. The old backend's data is left in place. Removing it needs the owner's yes.

## Switching the tracker

No command does this in this version. Show a preview: each item, where it
goes, and what cannot move (for example Notion card history). Move items only
with the owner's yes, one by one, reading each back. Then
`toolkit config set tracker.type <tracker>` and `toolkit doctor`.

## A new computer

1. `toolkit machine-setup` writes the Codex wrapper and the plugin-root
   pointer, and checks for `node`, `git`, `ntn`, `ollama`, and Hindsight.
2. `toolkit doctor` in each project.
3. The local tracker (`.work-items/`) and built-in memory (`.memory/`) are
   Git-ignored, so they do not come with a clone. After the owner copies the
   backup folder over, restore them with
   `toolkit import --from <backup-folder>/project` (a project export holds
   both folders). A memory-only backup made with the memory export goes back
   with `toolkit memory import --from <backup-folder>/memory`. Hindsight
   memory lives on the old Mac; move it the same way, through a memory
   export there and a memory import here. Notion needs no restore.
4. Owner steps on the new computer: `ntn login` (for Notion projects), and
   trusting the hooks in Codex (`/hooks`).

# The setup interview

Detail for `project-setup` step 2. Ask one question per message. Each
question carries a recommendation and its main reason, so the owner can
answer "yes" and move on.

## Look before asking

Check these first, without asking:

- Is this folder a Git repository? (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.) No
  repository: say so and offer `git init`. Toolkit V2 finds the project, the
  tracker, and memory through Git.
- Is the repository empty, or does it already hold code? Name the language
  and framework you see.
- `sfdx-project.json` present: this is a Salesforce project. Confirm it in
  one line instead of asking.
- `.toolkit.json` present with `"toolkit": "toolkit-v2"`: this is a repair,
  not a new setup (see `repair-and-wiring.md`).
- Files from an older toolkit setup (for example a `knowledge/` folder, or a
  `CLAUDE.md` with more than the line `@AGENTS.md`): tell the owner what you
  found. Toolkit V2 adds its own
  files and turns the current toolkit's plugins off for this project; it does
  not move or delete the old files. Ask before touching them. A file the
  project already has is kept, never overwritten.
- The owner name: `git config user.name`.
- `ntn whoami` (only matters for Notion): signed in or not.
- `toolkit hindsight health` (only matters for Hindsight): the local server is
  up or not.

## Question 1: the project name

Confirm the name, key, id prefix, and owner in one line:

> I'll call this project "Acme CRM" (short key `acme-crm`, work item ids `WI-001`, `WI-002`, owner Mike). Is that right?

- The key is the name in lowercase words joined by hyphens. It names the
  Hindsight memory bank and appears in the Notion page title.
- The id prefix is `WI` unless the owner wants another (for example `ACME`).
  A different prefix is set right after init, before any item exists, with
  `toolkit config set tracker.idPrefix <prefix>`.

## Question 2: where work is tracked

> Where should work items live? I recommend local folders on this computer: they are the fastest, work offline, and need nothing else set up. Choose Notion if you want to see and change the board on your phone or the web. GitHub Issues and Jira are possible, but the toolkit only gives written instructions for them.

| Choice | `--tracker` | Good when | What to know |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Local folders | `local` | A solo project on one computer | Items live in `.work-items/`, which Git ignores. They stay on this computer; `toolkit export` is the backup. |
| Notion | `notion` | The owner wants the board on his phone or the web | Needs `ntn` signed in. Each project gets its own Work Items and Memory databases under the "AI Agent Second Brain" page. |
| GitHub Issues | `github` | The code and the team already live in GitHub | No driver: agents follow written instructions with `gh`. Labels are created once, with a yes. |
| Jira | `jira` | A client requires Jira | No driver: agents follow written instructions with the Jira tool the owner connects. |

## Question 3: where memory lives

> Where should the project's memory live? I recommend the built-in `.memory/` folder: it is private, fast, and needs no server. [When the tracker is Notion: I recommend Notion, so work and memory sit together and you can read both on your phone.] Hindsight is also installed on this Mac; choose it if you want search by meaning across many memories.

| Choice | `--memory` | Good when | What to know |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Built-in `.memory/` | `builtin` | Most projects | Files in the main checkout, Git-ignored, on this computer only; the `memory-tidy` skill backs it up to a folder the owner picks. |
| Local Hindsight | `hindsight` | Many memories, and search by meaning matters | The local server at `127.0.0.1:8888` must be running (a background service on this Mac). One memory bank per project. Never Hindsight Cloud. |
| Notion | `notion` | The tracker is Notion, or the owner reads memory on his phone | The project's Memory database in Notion. Needs `ntn` signed in. |

Recommendation rule: Notion when the tracker is Notion; otherwise built-in.

## Question 4: Salesforce

Skip the yes-or-no question when `sfdx-project.json` answered it; confirm in
one line instead.

> Is this a Salesforce project? I recommend no, because I found no `sfdx-project.json`. A yes adds the Salesforce rules, the deploy and data-change skills, the protected-org guards, and the `delivery/` folder.

For a Salesforce project, ask for the org aliases, one question at a time.
Show the aliases on this computer first (`sf org list`, a read-only command):

> Which org alias is the sandbox the agents may deploy to for testing? I see `acme-uat` and `acme-dev`; I recommend `acme-uat`.

> Which org alias is production? Agents never deploy there or change its data; the guards block it and hand you the command instead. I see `acme-prod`.

Record them after init:

```text
toolkit config set salesforce.orgs.sandbox <alias>
toolkit config set salesforce.orgs.production <alias>
```

## After the answers

Say what will happen in three or four lines, then run it:

> I'll now copy the model scaffold and apply your answers: the project's folders and files from the model project, AGENTS.md with only the parts for your choices, the rules, and the settings; turn on the Toolkit V2 plugins for this project only (and turn the older toolkit's plugins off here); set up local folders for work and built-in memory. Nothing outside this folder changes.

Then `toolkit init`, the `toolkit config set` lines the answers need, the
wiring in `repair-and-wiring.md`, filling the setup guides (below), and
`toolkit doctor`.

## What setup installs

The toolkit plugin carries an exact copy of the model project in its
`scaffold/model/` folder. Setup copies that model and applies the answers:

| Installed | When |
| --- | --- |
| `AGENTS.md`, `PROJECT.md`, `PROJECT-ROADMAP.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `README.md`, `.gitignore` | Every project |
| `SOUL.md` | Every project, unless the owner declines it (`--decline SOUL.md`, or `toolkit config set declined SOUL.md` later) |
| `requirements/` (its own `AGENTS.md`, `SYSTEM-DATA-MODEL.md`, and `system-area-template/`), `system-guide/AREA-TEMPLATE.md`, `tests/TEST-PLAN-TEMPLATE.md`, `ai-external-knowledge/INDEX.md` | Every project |
| The general rules in `.claude/rules/` | Every project (Codex reads them through `AGENTS.md`) |
| A root `CLAUDE.md` holding only `@AGENTS.md`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/output-styles/plain-english.md` | Claude Code is one of the hosts |
| `.codex/config.toml` and `.codex/rules/toolkit.rules` (written by the toolkit; the model has neither) | Codex is one of the hosts |
| `.work-items/work-item-template/` (`WORK-ITEM.md`, `DESIGN.md`) and `.claude/rules/work-item-folders.md` | Local folders tracker |
| `.memory/` seed files: `AGENTS.md`, `CURRENT_FOCUS.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `memory-criteria.md`, `project_topic_template.md`, `terminology-glossary.md` | Built-in memory |
| `delivery/`, `sfdx-project.json`, `.forceignore`, `tools/kb/`, `tools/permissions/`, the two guard hooks in `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/protected-orgs.json`, and the nine Salesforce rules | Salesforce projects |
| The `sf-*` skills in `.claude/skills/` | Salesforce projects with Claude Code as a host |
| `.codex/hooks.json` (runs the two guard hooks in Codex) and the `sf-*` skills in `.agents/skills/` | Salesforce projects with Codex as a host |

- `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, and `PROJECT.md` carry setup markers such as
  `<!-- if tracker=local -->` ... `<!-- endif -->`. Setup keeps the lines for
  the answers given and removes the rest, markers included.
- The rules list in `AGENTS.md`, between `<!-- toolkit:rules:start -->` and
  `<!-- toolkit:rules:end -->`, is written from the files in `.claude/rules/`
  and rebuilt on every `toolkit sync`. Never edit it by hand.
- In a project that is not a Salesforce project, the Salesforce hooks and
  `sf` permission lines are left out of `.claude/settings.json`, and the
  Salesforce lines are left out of `.gitignore`.
- `.memory/MEMORY.md` is generated: setup installs the model's copy, then
  `toolkit memory reindex` rebuilds it.
- Setup never copies work items or memory records, and never copies the
  model's `.vscode/` or `.sfdx/` folders.
- `.toolkit.json` records the answers. It is written last.

## Filling the setup guides

The copied files start with a fill-in guide comment and hold `<angle bracket>`
prompts. Setup fills the project name. The rest is the agent's, with facts the
owner confirmed:

- `AGENTS.md`: the one-sentence outcome, and the "Build, test, or deploy" row
  under Commands. Ask for both, one question at a time, with a
  recommendation from what the repository shows.
- `PROJECT.md` and `README.md`: follow each file's guide. Ask only what the
  repository cannot answer.
- `PROJECT-ROADMAP.md` (the project outcome, phases, and work units) and
  `requirements/SYSTEM-DATA-MODEL.md` (accepted data model requirements):
  fill them when the owner already knows the facts. On a new project they
  usually stay as they are, and are listed in the final report as prompts
  left. The data model gets only accepted requirements, never a guess.
- `SOUL.md`: ask whether the owner wants it ("Do you want a SOUL.md that tells
  the agent how you like to work? I recommend skipping it for now; you can add
  it later."). Ask it with the other setup questions, so a no goes to init as
  `--decline SOUL.md` and the file is never installed. With a yes, fill it with
  his words and get his approval. A no after init: run
  `toolkit config set declined SOUL.md`, then delete the file. The no is kept
  in `.toolkit.json`, so sync never brings the file back and doctor does not
  report it missing. `toolkit config set declined none` undoes it.
- Delete each fill-in guide once its file is filled. Never invent a fact to
  fill a prompt: list each prompt that is left, with the fact it needs, in the
  final report.

## Explaining the result

End with a short plain report:

- What was set up, as a short list the owner can check: tracker, memory,
  Salesforce or not, the files added.
- What was skipped and why.
- What the owner must do himself (see the SKILL.md list), each with why.
- Doctor's result: clean, or each remaining problem with its fix.
- One next step: "Tell me the first thing you want built."
